newsitem.title: USA: Texas energy regulator ahead in re-election bid.
newsitem.headline: Texas energy regulator ahead in re-election bid.

text.p: The head of the Texas agency regulating oil and natural gas production in the state has "incumbency and big money" on her side in her bid for re-election, political analysts said.

Republican Carole Keeton Rylander, chairman of the Texas Railroad Commission, has raised about $1.4 million -- much of it from the oil and gas industry -- to finance her statewide campaign, analysts said.

"I am working for energy independence, replacing foreign crude with Texas oil and gas," Rylander says in television ads featuring the petite regulator standing with two burly oilfield workers at her side and striding through a Texas oilfield.
Her Democratic opponent, former state senator Hector Uribe, has raised about $40,000, plans no television advertising and is running on a platform of abolishing the legendary commission.

With President Bill Clinton and GOP challenger Bob Dole in a virtual dead heat in Texas and Sen. Phil Gramm staving off an inspired challenge by high school civics teacher Victor Morales in statewide voting, the commission race has been largely ignored by voters and pundits in the Lone Star state.
A recent Houston Chronicle poll showed Rylander leading Uribe 35 percent to 20 percent, with a large undecided vote.
